Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:11:1.english: If one who is not commanded and performs [it] — so - The Holy One, blessed be He, paid him his reward.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:12:1.hebrew: הא דר' יהודה - דאמר סומא פטור מן המצות, בב"ק פרק החובל (בבא קמא דף פז.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:12:1.english: This [statement] of Rabbi Yehuda - In which he said that a blind person is exempt from the mitzvot, [is taught] in Bava Kamma, in the chapter [entitled] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 87a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:12:2.english: A festive day for the rabbis - A feast for the students.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:12:3.english: I am not commanded - For he was blind.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:13:1.english: Once [he] was wearing - Dama ben Netina.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:13:2.hebrew: סירקון - לבוש שקורין צינד"ר (צינדי"ר: מין משי):
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:13:2.english: Sirkon - A garment called cendre (cender: a type of silk).

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:13:3.english: Of gold - Embroidered with gold thread.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:14:1.hebrew: פסיוני - עוף חשוב ושמן, מין שליו שירד במדבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:14:1.english: Pheasant - A prized and fat bird, a species of quail that fell in the wilderness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:14:2.hebrew: וטורדו מן העולם - שנענש עליו, שמראה לו צרות עין על סעודתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:14:2.english: And drives him from the world - That [the son] is punished on his account, as he displays begrudgingness toward him over his meal:

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:14:3.english: And there is [one] who makes him grind with a millstone - Which is difficult work.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:1:1.hebrew: משדלתו - מפתה אותו, כדמתרגמינן: ״וכי יפתה״ (שמות כב) — ״ארי ישדל״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:1:1.english: She persuades him - She entices him, as we translate [in the Targum]: “And if [a man] entices” (Exodus 22:15) — “Ari yeshadal.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:2:1.hebrew: והארץ הדום רגלי - והעובר בסתר אומר: ״אין המקום כאן״, לפיכך הוא נסתר לומר: ״אין יודע״. נמצא כדוחק רגליו ומקצרו, לומר: ״אין כאן״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:2:1.english: And the earth is My footstool - And one who transgresses in secret says, “The Omnipresent is not here”; therefore he hides, saying, “No one knows.” Consequently, he is like one who pushes away His feet and curtails [His footstool], saying, “[He] is not here.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:3:1.hebrew: מלא כל הארץ - משמע: משתרבב ויורד למטה, והזוקף קומתו נראה כדוחק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:3:1.english: The entire world is full [of His glory] - This implies that [His glory] extends and descends downward, and one who straightens his posture appears as though he is crowding [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:4:1.hebrew: אמר לו כך - ר' יהושע השיב לו כדרך שהשיב לו ר' אליעזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:4:1.english: He said this to him - Rabbi Yehoshua replied to him in the same manner that Rabbi Eliezer replied to him.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:1.hebrew: נתגרשה - שאין אמי חייבת בכבוד אבי, מהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:1.english: [If] she is divorced - Since my mother is not obligated in the honor of my father, what is [the law]?

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:2.hebrew: מבין ריסי עיניך - שערות שבשורות כסוי העין. אתה ניכר שהיית יתום, ונשרו ריסי עיניך מן הבכי, כדאמרי' [בסנהדרין] (ד' קד:): "והיה רבן גמליאל שומע קולה ובוכה כנגדה, עד שנשרו ריסי עיניו":
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:2.english: From between the eyelashes of your eyes - [These are] the hairs in the rows of the covering of the eye. It is evident from you that you were an orphan, and your eyelashes fell out from weeping, as we say [in Sanhedrin] (104b): “And Rabban Gamliel would hear her voice and weep along with her, until the eyelashes of his eyes fell out.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:3.hebrew: שבן אלמנה אתה - ולא צריך אתה למעשה, אלא ללמוד באת; ואני אומר לך שכבוד שניהם שוה עליך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:3.english: That you are the son of a widow - And you do not need [this] for practical application; rather, you came [only] to learn. And I tell you that the honor of both of them is equal upon you.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:4.hebrew: הטל להם מים בספל וקעקע - קרקר להם, כמו שמקרקרין לתרנגולים. ולפי שלא היה צריך לעשות, והוא שאלו כמו שעליו לעשות: ״אמר לי אבא ואימא״ — השיבו בלשון שחוק:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:5:4.english: Pour water for them into a pitcher and squawk - Cluck to them, as one clucks to chickens. And because he did not need to act [upon it], yet he asked him as though it were incumbent upon him to act — [saying,] “Father and Mother said to me” — [Rabbi Yehoshua] answered him in jest.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:7:1.hebrew: חזרו והודו למאמרות הראשונות - כ"ש שחייב אדם בכבודו, שאף הוא שותף בבריאתו כאביו ואמו, וחייו ומותו מסורין בידו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:7:1.english: They returned and conceded to the first statements - [Saying:] All the more so is a person obligated to honor Him, for He too is a partner in his creation, like his father and mother, and his life and death are placed in His hands.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:7:2.hebrew: ראש דברך אמת - לא הוזקק הכתוב לומר ״ראש דברך אמת״, אלא לפי שהיו מרננים אחר דבריו הראשונים, לומר: ״לכבודו הזהיר״, ולאחר זמן חזרו והודו. כששמעו סוף דבריו, למדו שראש דבריו אמת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:7:2.english: “The beginning of Your word is truth” - The verse only needed to say “The beginning of Your word is truth” because they were murmuring about His first statements, saying, “He commanded for His own honor”; and later on they retracted and conceded. When they heard the end of His statements, they learned that the beginning of His statements was truth.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:8:1.english: For six hundred thousand profit - He would have profited from it six hundred thousand gold dinars.

Rashi on Kiddushin 31a:8:2.english: Under his father's head - And he was sleeping.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:11:1.hebrew: גדול המצווה ועושה - נראה דהיינו טעמא דמי שמצווה ועושה עדיף: לפי שדואג ומצטער יותר פן יעבור ממי שאין מצווה, שיש לו פת בסלו — שאם ירצה יניח:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:11:1.english: "Greater is one who is commanded and performs" - It appears that this is the reason that one who is commanded and performs [a mitzvah] is superior: because he worries and is more distressed lest he transgress than one who is not commanded, who has "bread in his basket" — for if he wishes, he can leave [it].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:12:1.hebrew: דלא מפקידנא ועבדינא - מכאן מדקדק ר"ת דנשים מברכות על מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא. אע"ג דפטורות לגמרי — דאפילו מדרבנן לא מיחייבי, כדמוכח פרק מי שמתו (ברכות דף כ:) — מ"מ יכולות הן לברך, ואין כאן משום "לא תשא את שמו לשוא" (שמות כ׳:ז׳) משום מברכות ברכה שאינה צריכה. דאי לאו הכי, היכי שמח רב יוסף? והלא מפסיד כל הברכות כולן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:12:1.english: "As I am not commanded and yet I perform" - From here Rabbeinu Tam deduces that women may recite a blessing over time-bound positive commandments. Even though they are completely exempt — for even rabbinically they are not obligated, as is demonstrated in the chapter [entitled] "Mi Shemeito" (Berakhot 20b) — nevertheless they may recite a blessing, and there is no [violation] here of "You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain" (Exodus 20:7) on account of reciting an unnecessary blessing. For if that were not so, how could Rav Yosef have rejoiced? Would he not be losing all of the blessings?

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:13:1.english: "And his mother came and tore it" - It is [stated] in the Midrash that she was mentally deranged.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:14:1.hebrew: יש מאכיל לאביו פסיוני - פירוש: עוף חשוב, והיינו מין שליו שיש במדבר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:14:1.english: "There is one who feeds his father pheasant" - Explanation: A prized bird, and this is a species of quail that is in the wilderness.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:14:2.hebrew: וטורדו מן העולם - פירוש: שנענש עליו, שמראה לו צר עין על סעודתו. ו"יש מטחינו בריחים", שהיא מלאכה קשה — ומביאו לחיי העולם הבא, שמכבדו בדברים טובים ונחומים. ובגמרת ירושלמי (פאה פ"א) גרסינן מעשה בשניהם: מעשה באחד שהיה מאכיל לאביו פסיוני; פעם אחת אמר לו אביו: "מאין לך כל אלה?" אמר לו: "סבא, מאי איכפת לך? עד דטחון ואכול!" כלומר: לעוס ואכול, כעין כלבים דמדשין ואוכלים. א"כ הראהו שקשה עליו. ושוב מעשה באחד שהיה טוחן בריחים, ואב זקן היה לו, ואתא ציווי לטוחנין — פירוש: מצות המלך — בשביל אביו לבא לעבודת המלך. א"ל בנו: "טחון, ואני אלך תחתיך לעבודת המלך שאין לה קצבה; אם לבזיונך — טב לך, ואם למלקי — טב לך":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:14:2.english: "And causes him to be removed from the World" - Explanation: That [the son] is punished for it, because he displays a begrudging attitude toward him regarding his meal. And [as for the statement,] "and there is one who makes him grind with a millstone," which is difficult labor — [yet] it brings him [i.e., the son] to the life of the World-to-Come, because he honors him with kind and comforting words. And in the Gemara of the Yerushalmi (Peah, ch. 1) we learn an incident regarding both of them: An incident occurred with one who would feed his father pheasant; one time his father said to him, "From where do you have all these?" He said to him, "Old man, what do you care? Just grind and eat!" That is to say: Chew and eat, like dogs that crush [their food] and eat. Thus he showed him that [providing for] him was burdensome to him. And again, an incident occurred with one who was grinding with a millstone, and he had an elderly father, and an order came for the millers — explanation: a royal decree — for his father to come to the service of the king. His son said to him, "Grind [here], and I will go in your place to the service of the king, which has no fixed limit; whether for humiliation, it is better for you [that I go], and whether for lashes, it is better for you [that I endure them]."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:2:1.hebrew: כל העובר עבירה בסתר כאילו דוחק רגלי שכינה - היינו דמצי כייף ליצריה, וכדמוכח פרק קמא דחגיגה (דף טז.):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:2:1.english: "Anyone who transgresses in secret, it is as though he pushes away the feet of the Divine Presence" - This is [specifically in a case] where he is able to subdue his [evil] inclination, as is proven in the first chapter of Chagigah (16a).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:7:1.hebrew: כבד את ה' מהונך - בירושלמי דורש: "מהונך" כמו "מחונך". משמע שהקפיד הקב"ה על כיבוד אב ואם יותר מכבודו; שבכבודו הוא אומר: "כבד את ה' מהונך", דהיינו מחונך, דמשמע ממה שחננך — כלומר: אם יש לו ממון חייב, ואם לאו פטור; ובכיבוד אב ואם נאמר: "כבד את אביך ואת אמך", דמשמע בין שיש לו ממון ובין שאין לו, והיכא דלית ליה — חייב לחזר על הפתחים לזון את אביו ואת אמו:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:7:1.english: “Honor the Lord with your wealth” - In the Yerushalmi, it expounds “mehonecha” [with your wealth] like “mechonecha” [from that with which He was gracious to you]. This implies that the Holy One, Blessed be He, was more exacting regarding honoring father and mother than regarding His own honor; for regarding His own honor, He says: “Honor the Lord with your wealth,” which is [interpreted as] mechonecha, which implies from that which He has graciously granted you — that is to say, if he has money, he is obligated, and if not, he is exempt; whereas regarding honoring father and mother, it is stated: “Honor your father and your mother,” which implies whether he has money or does not have [money], and where he does not have [money], he is obligated to beg from door to door to sustain his father and his mother.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:8:1.hebrew: והיה מפתח מונח תחת מראשותיו של אביו - בירושלמי יש שהיו רגליו פשוטות על התיבה, ולכך לא שיברה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 31a:8:1.english: "And the key was placed under his father's head" - In the Yerushalmi it is [stated] that his [father's] feet were outstretched over the chest, and therefore he did not break it.
